_comment: Intake stub for the original Discrete 4 (USB PID 0xa270). This is NOT the Discrete 4 Synergy Core (0xa2be, discrete_4_sc.json) and nothing from that profile, Zen Go or Orion is assumed to apply. Every feature is disabled until this device's own captures confirm it. See docs/linux-parity-plan.md.

device.name: Antelope Discrete 4
device.notes: vid/pid/bcdDevice and product string "Discrete4" read from the attached unit's USB device descriptor (macOS IORegistry / system_profiler, 2026-11-16). Device class 0xEF/0x02/0x01 (interface association), bcdUSB 2.00, high speed, one configuration. Serial deliberately not recorded.

inputs.label: Inputs
inputs.status: disabled -- no command or state mapping captured on this device

usb_interfaces.notes: Interface classes from the device's own descriptors; endpoints from lsusb -v on Linux (iso EP 0x05 OUT / 0x84 IN, wMaxPacketSize 0x0a70; HID interrupt EP 0x01 OUT / 0x82 IN, 320 bytes).
usb_interfaces.evidence: owner's unit, macOS ioreg + Linux lsusb -v, 2026-11-16

transport.notes: From the device's own descriptors: HID v1.11 on interface 3, interrupt EP 0x01 OUT + 0x82 IN, wMaxPacketSize 320, bInterval 6 (4 ms at high speed). Report descriptor (54 bytes, usage page 0xFFA0) is byte-identical to the owner's Zen Go: one Input and one Output report of 320 bytes, NO report ID, no Feature report; GET_FEATURE / GET_REPORT(Input) STALL (EPIPE). Whether hidraw writes need a leading 0x00 report-number byte is not yet tested. Report magics and the command frame are not captured yet. The vendor manager-server log names in-band requests 0x74 / responses 0x75 for this unit (hint only).
transport.evidence: owner's unit on Linux 7.2: lsusb -v and tools/hid_probe.py, 2026-11-16

command.notes: No outbound command captured. Do not assume any sibling's 0x70 / opcode / param-id layout.

state_report.notes: The device streams two unsolicited 320-byte reports at ~125 Hz each with no host traffic: magic 0x73 (state) and 0x83 (meter-like, mostly 0x60/0x32 lanes), the same pair as Zen Go. Unlike Zen Go, bytes 4..5 of 0x73 are 0x0000 (Zen Go: 0x4001). With the device at 48 kHz, 0x73 bytes 22..23 = 0xbb80 (48000) and byte 18 = 0x02 (the family's 48k index): candidates only, not tested against a rate change. Over 10 s idle, 0x73 offsets 160-163, 224-227, 242-243 moved. Base offsets deliberately not filled in.
state_report.evidence: owner's unit, tools/readback_probe.py phase 1 (passive, 10 s), 2026-11-16; raw output kept privately

intake_hints.notes: Readback requests the vendor panel issued on connect, as printed (names + category/index) in the vendor's own runtime logs on the owner's Mac, 2026-11-13..16. They are hints for planning captures ONLY. They are not device-derived category_counts and must not be used as query bounds (PROTOCOL.md §4a hazard). Confirm each with a usbmon capture of the vendor connect walk before adding frame.readback.
intake_hints.audio_streaming: Linux 7.2 snd-usb-audio, no quirk (/proc/asound stream0, 2026-11-16): playback iface 1 EP 0x05 OUT async, capture iface 2 EP 0x84 IN async (also the playback sync EP), both S24_3LE x 16 ch, rates 32000/44100/48000/88200/96000/176400/192000, 125 us packets. 2 s record and silent playback at 48 kHz succeeded. Other rates untested.

channels.notes: Preamp count not yet established from this device's reports.
